notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (gate exit 0; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 model (run retriage-drivers-1-037) and reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no upstream evogym run, sim backend, ROS graph or device run is claimed. The card's entry symbol evogym.envs.walk:WalkingFlat was confirmed at evogym/envs/walk.py:15, and Walker-v0 is registered at evogym/envs/__init__.py:16-20. The package uses the card's GymnasiumDriver: cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action:{values}}, cap.world.reset.v1 takes {seed, options}, and cap.world.seed.v1 takes {seed}. The bridge derives the step action bounds from the fake's Box(0.6, 1.6) and action_space_ref cites evogym/envs/walk.py:36, the upstream line that defines the space.

THE FAKE IS AN F0 ANALYTIC STAND-IN, not a recording and not the upstream simulator. It moves one centre of mass at a placeholder gain from the mean clipped actuator value and holds four placeholder material points; it models neither the C++ point-mass soft-body physics, actuator deformation, contacts, collisions, constraint solving nor the self-collision instability, and there is no rendering. It uses a placeholder 5x5 body with one horizontal actuator, so the action width is 1 placeholder actuator and the derived action.values bound is [0.6]..[1.6] from the cited upstream line; the upstream body is a required WalkingFlat.__init__ argument (walk.py:17-27) and may have any valid shape and actuator count. The fake's observation has 10 values (2 + 2*4 placeholder points); the real size is 2 + num_robot_points (walk.py:34), where num_robot_points comes from the compiled simulator and the body, and is not reproduced. The fake applies the 500-step TimeLimit that gymnasium.make adds to Walker-v0 (registry line 19); WalkingFlat.step itself always returns truncated=False (walk.py:72). The fake ignores reset seed and options, matching EvoGymBase.reset (base.py:65-69); the bridge still advertises cap.world.seed.v1 because the reset signature accepts seed, and the fidelity contract states determinism exact with seed_control none and explains that the value does not change the initial state.

NO SIM BACKEND IS DECLARED and the upstream environment was not run: it needs Python >=3.7,<3.11 (pyproject.toml:40), gymnasium and numpy<2.0.0 (pyproject.toml:46-49), and the compiled CMake extension evogym.simulator_cpp (setup.py:61-65); gym.make('Walker-v0') also needs a robot body ndarray, which this package does not statically supply. The gate runs on Python 3.14 without gymnasium or evogym, and package code never imports the clone. The real simulator, its actual timestep and observation size, any trajectory, and any comparison with the fake remain unvalidated. NOT COVERED: the real evogym simulator and its compiled extension; the upstream body argument and the other registered environment classes (only Walker-v0 with WalkingFlat is served); the full observation array (the fake returns 10 placeholder values); rendering; snapshot and restore; and any hardware backend. The fake's action width and observation size are placeholder test data, not Facts or Limits. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, all catalogue classes.

WARNINGS left by the last gate run, all expected or explained: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the next reset and makes no native call; PLAYBOOK section 8 expects this for a Gymnasium driver); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for close because the gate's AST surface does not follow walk.py:8 'from evogym.envs import BenchmarkBase', although EvoGymBase is defined in the clone at evogym/envs/base.py:381 and defines close at evogym/envs/base.py:118, so the native class and the fake's close are correct; G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.values and seed twice (PLAYBOOK section 8 expects these simulator-family warnings). There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. The clone at 91c05ab7a793f86e099c21d377f183c95c9990cd was read only and G1 reports it unmodified; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review compared the Walker-v0 contract, every source citation, fake behavior, stop latch, provenance and MIT license with the pinned clone. Corrected coordinate-row flattening and Box dtype in fake.py and the regression in test_driver.py; driver.py removes upstream attribution from the placeholder-width fake action space and corrects the array dtype disclosure, with the matching facts.md update. Regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; fake G1-G9 and strict collection pass, with evidence limited to contract_checked. For the human reviewer: Only the F0 fake is served. The real WalkingFlat requires a robot body, a compiled C++ extension and Python <3.11; no deployment factory or simulator run is included. Its instability path also prints to stdout (walk.py:62-64), which needs handling before a stdio deployment.
